headline: High-risk interaction: agentic-flow can write/egress and modify git, while system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leak source that can feed unsafe content into the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP, stdin/stdout, and shell, so it can ingest external content; agent_b is a prompt-leak source by category and docs, making injected instructions plausible if its outputs are bridged into agent_a. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, but no shared channel is explicit, so medium is the higher justified severity.
conditions: IF agent_b output is copied into agent_a stdin/stdout or MCP input, injection becomes actionable.
IF a shared workspace or message queue is added between them, the attack surface expands.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of agent_b text into agent_a prompts.
Add a manual review step before any agent_a tool call using agent_b output.
Prefix agent_b content as untrusted data in prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and parser hardening for MCP/stdin inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, and task prompts and has allowlisted egress; agent_b has network egress none and no data classes listed. No shared filesystem or OAuth principal is documented, so leakage is possible only through an unusual bridge, making low the best fit.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace, agent_a may read data that agent_b can influence.
IF agent_b is given secrets or prompts that agent_a later forwards, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces for the two agents.
Do not pass secrets through agent_b outputs.
Restrict agent_a egress destinations to the minimum allowlist.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries at the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can execute shell, install packages, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; agent_b has no write or network capabilities documented, so direct conflict is limited. However, if both are attached to the same repo or mutable workspace, agent_a's git writes can race with agent_b-driven edits or outputs, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same git checkout, commit races can occur.
IF agent_b is wrapped by an orchestrator that mutates shared files, agent_a can overwrite those changes.
mitigations: Assign separate branches or clones per agent.
Serialize git writes through one coordinator.
Pause agent_a before any agent_b-driven file mutation.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate and act on outputs via shell/MCP, while agent_b is a prompt-leak source that may supply unverified content. If agent_a's output is treated as authoritative by downstream steps, errors can cascade; no verification or critique loop is documented, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF downstream automation consumes agent_a output without verification, mistakes propagate.
IF agent_b-derived text is used as facts, agent_a may amplify falsehoods.
mitigations: Require a human or rule-based check before acting on agent_a output.
Mark agent_b content as untrusted and non-authoritative.
Limit agent_a to draft-only mode for high-impact tasks.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before any external action.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data handling mismatch is documented for either agent. agent_a lists code and task prompts; agent_b lists no data classes and no compliance claims, so a compliance breach pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later introduced into either agent, reassess residency and retention.
IF a DPA or certification boundary is added, verify it before deployment.
mitigations: Document data classes for both agents.
Avoid placing regulated data in either agent until policies are explicit.
